content.text: No Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalties, or early-termination/minimum fees appear anywhere in the agreement. I'll submit a compliant finding.

input.quote: Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination.
input.rationale: The agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, kill fee, minimum-fee or early-termination charge payable by Clear Capital. Termination under § 6(a) (convenience, only when no SOW is outstanding) and § 6(b), and the repeated § 7(c) wind-down provision, entitle Contractor only to fees and expenses actually incurred or earned through the termination date — an accrued-amounts obligation, not a liquidated amount. Section 3 sets time-and-materials compensation, taxes and expense reimbursement with no late-payment penalty or interest, and § 7 caps each party's liability at fees paid rather than imposing any stipulated damages on us. This meets the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), so no redline is warranted. Noted only for completeness: § 3(b) lets Contractor change rates on 30 days' notice without a cap, but that is a pricing point addressed under other rules, not a Customer-payable liquidated damages issue.
